  "screen_decision": "include",
  "screen_rationale": "The study compares the concordance of drug toxicities between animal models (rat, dog) and human outcomes using a Liver-Chip system, reporting quantitative measures of toxicity prediction and species-specific differences. It directly addresses the agreement between animal results and human clinical outcomes for drug toxicities.",
  "arm": "toxicology",
  "arm_evidence": "Reproducing human and cross-species drug toxicities using a Liver-Chip. The study evaluates drug-induced liver injury (DILI) and compares toxicity prediction between animal models and humans.",
  "therapeutic_areas": [
    "hepatic",
    "cross-cutting"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "The study focuses on drug-induced liver injury (DILI) and uses a Liver-Chip model, directly relating to the hepatic therapeutic area. It also broadly assesses drug toxicity across species, fitting 'cross-cutting'.",
  "model_type": "across-multiple-models",
  "model_evidence": "The study utilizes rat, dog, and human Liver-Chips, comparing results across these species-specific models to assess concordance with human outcomes.",
  "species": [
    "rat",
    "dog"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "The study explicitly develops and tests rat, dog, and human Liver-Chips, comparing the predictive capacity of rat and dog models against human outcomes.",
  "endpoint_class": "mixed",
  "endpoint_evidence": "The study measures various endpoints including albumin secretion (biomarker), transaminase levels (biomarker), cell morphology, lipid accumulation (biomarker), ROS production (biomarker), and fibrosis markers (biomarker), alongside comparisons to clinical outcomes which can include hard endpoints."
